key_insight: A Lundgren spiral vortex ensemble links the head, body and tail of turbulence’s Q–R distribution to stretching, spiral arms and dissipation, respectively.
engineering_relevance: This physically interpretable framework could support synthetic turbulence generation and assessment of velocity-gradient statistics in turbulence models.
method: Construct woven Lundgren turbulence from a spiral vortex ensemble.
Vary background strain rate, vortex cutoff age and viscous decay factor.
Build an explicit P(Q,R) model combining stretching, spiral and dissipation contributions.
evidence_signal: Parameter sweeps show that stronger strain broadens the head, older vortex cutoffs increase body inclination and weaker viscous decay extends the tail; the explicit model is validated against WLT statistics.
watch_item: Validation described in the abstract uses synthetic WLT statistics; applicability to wall-bounded or anisotropic engineering flows remains unestablished.
paper_title: Modelling velocity gradient invariants in turbulence with Lundgren spiral vortex ensemble
